narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated a 65% chance that you will fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a risk estimate, not a certainty—it means roughly two in three applicants with a similar profile were predicted to fail—and the law school treated that level of risk as too high for admission. The strongest factor driving the prediction was your LSAT score of 21.30, which is far below the 37.18 average among accepted students; this pushed the decision most strongly toward likely bar failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.20 was the second-most influential factor. Because it is very close to the accepted-student average of 3.23, it worked in your favor and pushed toward likely success. The third-most influential factor was your third-year class standing of 2.00, well below the accepted average of 5.79; this also pushed toward likely bar failure. To improve future applications, focus first on raising your LSAT through structured preparation and a retake, since it was the dominant concern. Ask admissions for feedback, and consider strengthening your academic record or explaining any circumstances behind your third-year standing. Apply when your test score and recent academic evidence make a stronger case.
